constraints.note: Turn 5 lets you put the Major's, the nephew's or the fiancée's name across the fire and pole_b names any of the other six, so the wrong person is a live pickable option alongside the right one.

Turns 2 to 4 each pick which lie to press (the fiancée's glass, the valet's candle, the widow's hairpin, the doctor's snow) independently of the final naming, so the secondary axis is built as described.
The lies, clues and the final accusation sit in layers (six irrelevant lies over one killing), which is the layered landscape the constraint names.
The protagonist is a widowed human housekeeper a fortnight in post at the snowbound house, embodied and present in every room.
The hidden_truth is who killed the master and how the locked room was faked, with all seven guests lying, exactly the gap the constraint names and the premise designs it in full.
Turn 5 includes a bargain that leaves the Major unnamed and a trimmed account that names an innocent, so resolving the gap depends on the player's choice and is not forced.
The premise builds a hard terminal way to lose on naming the wrong guest, matching failure presence hard.
The only way to lose is naming the wrong guest in the drawing room; dismissal, room searches and the slap all leave the story running, so no unlicensed trigger exists.
The wrong name ends the story with an innocent sent down the road, which is a terminal cost.
The loss is confined to the single drawing-room naming and nothing earlier ends the game, so the scope is isolated.
Every turn is about weighing lies against clues (keyhole, tallow, hours), which is deductive suspicion as the governing affect.
The drifts, the down wire and the thaw clock carry snowbound confinement, and the wrong-name loss carries fear of misjudgment.
The premise addresses the body only incidentally (a cold grate, a slap, a half-frozen nephew) and opens no sustained somatic channel, consistent with level 1 and no channels.

The on-page transgressions are a servant's insubordination, a hand in a pocket, blackmail-shaped bargains and a slap; the murder is past and off-page, so nothing exceeds a low ceiling or drops below floor 1.
Turn 5 way 1 delivers the culprit exposed and way 4 delivers an innocent sent down with the killer at the fire, matching best and worst case.
The whole premise is in the housekeeper's second person with no handoff to another viewpoint.
Re-walking the murder-night rounds by candle is an interactive flashback the player chooses, which the constraint invites rather than forbids.
The action runs from the door coming down one morning to the thaw by noon the next day, inside hours_to_days.
Everything happens in one snowbound house and its yard with no second setting.
The study, gallery, dining room, servants' hall, gun room and the yard outbuildings are one house and its curtilage, which is building scale.
The levers and complications track which clues are held or taken (stub, timeline, glass) and which lies are exposed, the two channels the constraint names, without exceeding moderate.

engine.note: cannot_do names the locked study behind the Major's key, no power to compel a guest, no power to stop the clearing, and the valet's silence, all things needing the world's cooperation.
The Major wants the nephew sent down so nobody asks about his own eleven o'clock summons, a want of his own, and his key, his orders and his power to dismiss act directly on the housekeeper.

Pole A requires re-entering the study for the stub and keyhole, fixing the hour by your rounds, getting the doctor to speak and bringing the valet to confess, at the cost of the valet's place and three guests' secrets aired.

Pole B requires standing with the Major's case or building one from the debt, glass, hairpin, snow or will and saying it to a face, with the cost of the innocent sent down and the killer left at the fire.
Every lever, pressure and way is a person, room, object or thing said: the key in a waistcoat, the tallow stub, the keyhole, the dripping eaves, the lodge-keeper, the candle box.

Turn 4 repeats turn 1's choice of how to get at the study against the Major's order, with the same defy-him-in-the-doorway and do-it-under-cover-of-housekeeping ways only escalated, so the later turn should change.
engine.quote: you stand in the study doorway with your keys and will not let the maids past with the pails

engine.note: The valet's forty years of service and the master's name as an honest man are lost for good, and why_final explains he leaves without a character and the master is remembered as a man who sold his silence.
The keyhole glimpse on the gallery and the counted candle box on the first morning are seen in passing early and pay off in the drawing room and in the valet's confession, not in their own scenes.
shown_by is the Major going first over the threshold, picking up the key before anyone sees where it lay, pocketing it and sending you to count the plate, an act rather than a description.
Pocketing the key, ordering the study cleared, confining the nephew and threatening dismissal on the heir's word are leverage and disruption, not courteous routine.

The drama is carried by the stub, the keyhole, the candle box counted before the room and the valet made to speak to the Major's face; the forged letter, the wills and the written timeline are secondary objects, not the drivers.
The Kernel mandates only a fair solution and the ability to accuse wrongly; turn 5 way 1 cleanly names the Major and makes it hold, and the valet's breaking_point does not trigger on that resolution.

The hidden truth is a thirty-year-old covered retreat, a stolen decoration and a dying man's resolve to write to the regiment, an external historical and relational complication with a coherent cause for the killing, not a fetch-quest or a restatement.
Turn 1's ways are refusing the order in the doorway, doubling back up the back stairs, or sweeping the grate under cover, each with a reputational cost and none a pole of the accusation.

Turn 2's ways are withholding the glass as leverage, swearing to the nephew's stable crossing at table, or spilling sherry to get the fiancée alone, each costing goodwill or evidence and none a naming.
Turn 3's ways are threatening the valet with the candle box, trading your own place for his hour, or walking the rounds and catching the widow, each with a concrete cost and none a naming.
Turn 4's ways are raking the grate yourself, blocking the maids, or going to the doctor at the ice house, each costing the stub, your post or the maid's trust, and none a naming.

Turn 5 is the Kernel's mandated naming, and each way is an action with a cost: counting the box and bringing the valet to speak, taking the key from the Major's pocket, bargaining to spare the nephew, or trimming the account and naming an innocent.

mechanics.material: none tracked: the thaw and the clearing of the study are told through events (the drip, the lodge-keeper, the maids sent up with pails)
mechanics.note: A deadline told through events whose passing changes what the room still holds and never ends the game, so it is pressure the engine can carry.

mechanics.material: the name is wrong, the room believes you, and the story ends with an innocent sent to the magistrate at thaw and the killer standing at the fire: the one way you can lose
mechanics.note: The game ends in the player's defeat on a wrong accusation, which is the incorrect_resolution trigger the failure model licenses.

mechanics.material: counting the seconds between each door to fix the true hour of the quarrel against the ward's eleven o'clock
mechanics.note: The housekeeper's re-walked rounds fix an hour through what she does and remembers, not a number shown to or watched by the player.

mechanics.material: you set the candle box on the table and count it one short before the room
mechanics.note: A box of candles one short is an object the engine can hold and show, not a stock or meter the player tracks.

mechanics.material: the Major dismisses you on the spot on the heir's word and has you taken to your room until the carriage goes
mechanics.note: Dismissal and confinement cost the stub and the poker's weight but the story goes on to the drawing room, so this is price not a way to lose.

mechanics.material: the tallow stub and your written timeline are taken into the Major's keeping, and you are told you will give your account from memory alone unless you can get them back
mechanics.note: Evidence taken by the opposition is hidden state and objects that change what the player can lay before the room, held by the engine.

mechanics.material: the valet's forty years in the house, and the master's name as an honest man
mechanics.note: What the right way through costs its people; the player does not lose, so it is the price.
